views.name: customer_transaction_daily_effects
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_transactions.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(substr(customer_transactions.txn_date,1,10)) AS txn_date,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(customer_transactions.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN customer_transactions.txn_amount
    WHEN lower(customer_transactions.txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -customer_transactions.txn_amount
    ELSE -customer_transactions.txn_amount
  END AS signed_amount,
  CASE WHEN customer_transactions.txn_amount IS NOT NULL AND customer_transactions.txn_amount != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_activity
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: Normalize and canonicalize customer transactions into one row per customer per transaction date, with signed amount (deposits positive, withdrawals and unknown types negative) and parsed ISO date. Strips time component where present.

views.name: calendar_months_range
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  date(date(month_start, '+1 month', '-1 day')) AS month_end_date
FROM (
  SELECT date(min_txn, 'start of month') AS month_start
  FROM (
    SELECT MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn, MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn
    FROM customer_transactions
  )
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date(next_month, 'start of month') AS month_start
  FROM (
    SELECT date(min_txn, '+' || n || ' months') AS next_month, max_txn
    FROM (
      SELECT MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn, MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn
      FROM customer_transactions
    ), (
      SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
      UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11
      UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17
      UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23
      UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
      UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35
      UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41
      UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47
      UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49 UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53
      UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
    )
    WHERE date(min_txn, '+' || n || ' months') <= date(max_txn, 'start of month')
  )
)
GROUP BY month_start
views.description: Generate one row per calendar month (year, month) in the global date range of customer transactions. This view enumerates all months between the minimum txn_date and maximum txn_date found in customer_transactions and provides month_end_date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format. (Intended to be cross-joined to customers.)

views.name: customer_monthly_closing_candidates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.customer_id AS customer_id,
  m.year AS year,
  m.month AS month,
  m.month_end_date AS month_end_date,
  COALESCE(SUM(d.signed_amount) FILTER (WHERE strftime('%Y', d.txn_date) = printf('%04d', m.year) AND strftime('%m', d.txn_date) = printf('%02d', m.month)), 0) AS monthly_net_amount,
  MAX(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', d.txn_date) = printf('%04d', m.year) AND strftime('%m', d.txn_date) = printf('%02d', m.month) THEN d.has_activity ELSE 0 END) AS has_activity,
  COALESCE(COUNT(d.txn_date) FILTER (WHERE strftime('%Y', d.txn_date) = printf('%04d', m.year) AND strftime('%m', d.txn_date) = printf('%02d', m.month)), 0) AS month_txn_count
FROM
  calendar_months_range m
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transaction_daily_effects
) c
LEFT JOIN customer_transaction_daily_effects d
  ON d.customer_id = c.customer_id
    AND date(d.txn_date) <= date(m.month_end_date)
GROUP BY
  c.customer_id,
  m.year,
  m.month,
  m.month_end_date
views.description: For each customer_id and calendar month (year, month) that appears in the global months range, compute aggregated transaction totals in that month, whether the customer had activity, and the month-end cumulative transaction sum up through that month's last day (cumulative raw sum to be used to derive closing_balance). This view intentionally groups by customer_id, year, month to serve as the monthly-level building block for final closing balance, change and carry-forward logic.

views.name: customer_transactions_2020_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- normalize txn_date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD when possible; otherwise keep original
  (CASE
     WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-' AND substr(txn_date,8,1) = '-' THEN txn_date
     WHEN instr(txn_date,'/') = 3 AND instr(txn_date,'/') = 6 THEN
       -- format DD/MM/YY or D/M/YY -> attempt to convert to YYYY-MM-DD assuming 2-digit year -> treat as 2000+YY
       (printf('20%02d-%02d-%02d',
               cast(substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1, instr(substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1),'/')-1) AS INTEGER),
               cast(substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1, instr(substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1),'/')-1) AS INTEGER),
               cast(substr(txn_date,1, instr(txn_date,'/')-1) AS INTEGER)))
     WHEN instr(txn_date,'-') = 3 AND instr(txn_date,'-') = 6 THEN
       -- format DD-MM-YYYY or DD-MM-YY -> try to detect DD-MM-YYYY
       (CASE WHEN length(txn_date)=10 THEN
         (substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2))
       ELSE txn_date END)
     ELSE txn_date
   END) AS txn_date,
  -- txn_yyyy_mm as YYYY-MM from parsed ISO-like txn_date when possible, else NULL
  (CASE
     WHEN length(txn_date) >= 7 AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-' THEN substr(txn_date,1,7)
     WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,3,1) = '/' THEN
       -- assume DD/MM/YYYY -> YYYY-MM
       (substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2))
     WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,3,1) = '-' THEN
       -- assume DD-MM-YYYY -> YYYY-MM
       (substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2))
     ELSE NULL
   END) AS txn_yyyy_mm,
  -- signed amount: deposits positive, others negative; keep numeric txn_amount
  (CASE
     WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
     WHEN txn_amount IS NULL THEN NULL
     ELSE -txn_amount
   END) AS txn_amount_signed,
  txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized/cleaned transaction rows for customers with parsed ISO year-month and signed amounts where 'deposit' is positive and any other txn_type is treated as negative; also exposes txn_date normalized to YYYY-MM-DD when possible.

views.name: customer_monthly_month_end_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ctd.customer_id AS customer_id,
  printf('%04d-%02d', cmr.year, cmr.month) AS month_yyyy_mm,
  COALESCE(SUM(ctd.signed_amount), 0) AS month_end_balance
FROM
  calendar_months_range AS cmr
CROSS JOIN
  (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions) AS customers
LEFT JOIN
  customer_transaction_daily_effects AS ctd
  ON ctd.customer_id = customers.customer_id
  AND strftime('%Y-%m', ctd.txn_date) = printf('%04d-%02d', cmr.year, cmr.month)
GROUP BY
  customers.customer_id,
  cmr.year,
  cmr.month
views.description: Per-customer, per-calendar-month balance (month-end balance) computed as the sum of signed transaction amounts in that month. One row per customer per month where months are expressed as 'YYYY-MM'. Does not drop customers-months with no transactions (those can be produced by cross-join with customer list in question_ops).

views.name: distinct_customers
views.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  customer_id
FROM
  customer_transactions
views.description: List of distinct customers present in customer_transactions (one row per customer_id). Useful for including customers with zero transactions in a month by cross-joining to month domain.

views.name: customer_monthly_net_txn
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  -- month_start represented as the month's first day in YYYY-MM-01 format derived from txn_date
  substr(ct.txn_date,1,7) || '-01' AS month_start,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
      WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -ct.txn_amount
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS monthly_net
FROM customer_transactions ct
WHERE ct.txn_type IN ('deposit','withdrawal')
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, substr(ct.txn_date,1,7)
views.description: Per customer and calendar month (represented as the month's first day), compute the net transaction amount summing deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative. Excludes other txn_type values.

views.name: customer_monthly_closing_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cmn.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cmn.month_start AS month_start,
  cmn.monthly_net AS monthly_net,
  (
    SELECT SUM(c2.monthly_net)
    FROM customer_monthly_net_txn c2
    WHERE c2.customer_id = cmn.customer_id
      AND (strftime('%Y-%m-%d', c2.month_start) <= strftime('%Y-%m-%d', cmn.month_start))
  ) AS closing_balance
FROM customer_monthly_net_txn cmn
views.description: Per customer and month (month_start), compute cumulative closing balance over time by ordering months chronologically and doing running sum of monthly_net.

views.name: customer_most_recent_month_growth
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cmmcb.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cmmcb.month_start AS recent_month_start,
  cmmcb.closing_balance AS recent_closing_balance,
  COALESCE(prev.closing_balance, 0) AS previous_closing_balance,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(prev.closing_balance, 0) = 0 THEN COALESCE(cmmcb.closing_balance, 0) * 100.0
    ELSE (COALESCE(cmmcb.closing_balance, 0) - prev.closing_balance) / prev.closing_balance
  END AS growth_rate
FROM
  -- most recent month per customer from monthly closing balances
  (
    SELECT customer_id, month_start, closing_balance
    FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance c
    WHERE month_start = (
      SELECT MAX(month_start) FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance c2 WHERE c2.customer_id = c.customer_id
    )
  ) AS cmmcb
LEFT JOIN
  -- previous month closing balance (month immediately before recent_month_start)
  customer_monthly_closing_balance prev
ON prev.customer_id = cmmcb.customer_id
AND prev.month_start = (
  SELECT month_start
  FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance p2
  WHERE p2.customer_id = cmmcb.customer_id
    AND p2.month_start < cmmcb.month_start
  ORDER BY p2.month_start DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
views.description: For each customer, pick the most recent month (latest month_start with any transactions) and compute that month's growth versus the previous month's closing balance. Growth uses the rule: if previous closing balance = 0 then growth = current_closing_balance * 100, else growth = (current_closing_balance - previous_closing_balance) / previous_closing_balance.

views.name: customer_transaction_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- normalize txn_date to ISO YYYY-MM-DD where possible: assume input is already YYYY-MM-DD or similar; try substrings for common formats
  CASE
    WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 AND txn_date LIKE '%-%' THEN
      -- assume already YYYY-MM-DD or DD-MM-YYYY; disambiguate: if first four chars are year numeric -> keep
      CASE WHEN substr(txn_date,1,4) GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]' THEN txn_date
           -- if format is DD-MM-YYYY convert to YYYY-MM-DD
           WHEN substr(txn_date,3,1) = '-' AND substr(txn_date,6,1) = '-' THEN
             substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
           ELSE txn_date END
    WHEN txn_date LIKE '%/%' THEN
      -- handle formats like DD/MM/YY or DD/MM/YYYY or D/M/YY etc.
      -- try to parse as DD/MM/YYYY -> convert
      CASE
        WHEN length(txn_date) >= 8 AND substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1,1) GLOB '[0-9]' THEN
          -- split by '/' using simple substring functions: assume DD/MM/YYYY
          (CASE
             WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 THEN substr(txn_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(txn_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(txn_date,1,2)
             WHEN length(txn_date) = 8 THEN
               -- assume D/M/YY -> convert to 20YY with zero-pad
               '20' || substr(txn_date,7,2) || '-' || printf('%02d', CAST(substr(txn_date,4,1) AS INTEGER)) || '-' || printf('%02d', CAST(substr(txn_date,1,1) AS INTEGER))
             ELSE txn_date END)
        ELSE txn_date
      END
    ELSE txn_date
  END AS txn_date,
  txn_amount,
  txn_type
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: Row-level customer transaction records with txn_date normalized to ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) and raw txn_amount preserved. One row per transaction event. Useful as the base ledger for running-balance and monthly-cohort calculations.

views.name: customer_months
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start_date,
  MIN(txn_date) AS example_txn_date
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL AND trim(txn_date) <> ''
GROUP BY substr(txn_date, 1, 7)
views.description: Distinct months (month start) present in the customer_transactions table derived from txn_date. One row per calendar month present in data with an ordered month_start_date (YYYY-MM-01). Useful to enumerate month cutoffs and to exclude the earliest month as a baseline.

views.name: customer_running_balance_at_month_start
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  DATE(substr(ct.txn_date,1,4) || '-' || substr(ct.txn_date,6,2) || '-01') AS month_start_date,
  (
    SELECT IFNULL(SUM(txn_amount),0)
    FROM customer_transactions t2
    WHERE t2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
      AND DATE(t2.txn_date) < DATE(substr(ct.txn_date,1,4) || '-' || substr(ct.txn_date,6,2) || '-01')
  ) AS raw_balance
FROM customer_transactions ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, month_start_date
views.description: For each customer and for each calendar month present in customer_transactions, compute that customer's cumulative balance as of the first day of the month (i.e. sum of txn_amount for txn_date < month_start_date). One row per customer_id + month_start_date. Negative balances are not clamped in this view (raw_balance provided) so downstream queries can apply clamp-to-zero business rule.

views.name: customer_daily_end_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.txn_date AS calendar_date,
  (
    -- running sum of signed amounts up to and including this date
    SELECT IFNULL(SUM(ctde.signed_amount), 0)
    FROM customer_transaction_daily_effects ctde
    WHERE ctde.customer_id = d.customer_id
      AND DATE(ctde.txn_date) <= DATE(d.txn_date)
  ) AS end_of_day_balance
FROM
  customer_transaction_daily_effects d
views.description: Compute each customer's end-of-day running balance for every calendar date that should be present given transactions, carrying forward prior day's balance when there is no transaction that day. Treat txn_date as date (YYYY-MM-DD). Transaction effect: +txn_amount for txn_type='deposit', otherwise -txn_amount. The grain is one row per customer_id and calendar_date (end-of-day).

views.name: customer_30day_avg_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.calendar_date AS calendar_date,
  AVG(d2.end_of_day_balance) AS avg_30day_balance,
  CASE WHEN AVG(d2.end_of_day_balance) < 0 THEN AVG(d2.end_of_day_balance) ELSE AVG(d2.end_of_day_balance) END AS avg_30day_balance_nonnegative
FROM customer_daily_end_balance d
JOIN customer_daily_end_balance d2
  ON d.customer_id = d2.customer_id
  AND date(d2.calendar_date) BETWEEN date(d.calendar_date, '-29 days') AND date(d.calendar_date)
GROUP BY d.customer_id, d.calendar_date
HAVING COUNT(d2.end_of_day_balance) = 30
views.description: For each customer and calendar date compute the 30-day rolling average of end-of-day balances ending on that date. Only emit rows where the customer has 30 days of contiguous end-of-day balances (i.e., the current date and prior 29 calendar dates have defined end_of_day_balance). If the 30-day average is negative, downstream processing will treat it as zero (the view returns the raw average and a nonnegative_adjusted_avg column). Grain is one row per customer_id and calendar_date.

views.name: customer_monthly_max_30day_avg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(calendar_date,1,7) AS month,
  MAX(avg_30day_balance) AS max_30day_avg
FROM
  customer_30day_avg_balance
GROUP BY
  customer_id,
  substr(calendar_date,1,7)
views.description: For each customer and calendar month (YYYY-MM), return the maximum of that customer's daily 30-day averages that fall in that month. If a customer has no valid 30-day averages in the month, this view should still emit a row for the customer-month with max_30day_avg = 0 if requested by the final query (this view emits only months where a max exists from the 30-day view; final query can left-join to include zeros). Grain is one row per customer_id and month (YYYY-MM).

views.name: customer_daily_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 4) || '-' || substr(txn_date, 6, 2) || '-' || substr(txn_date, 9, 2) AS txn_date,
  txn_amount AS txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized per-customer per-transaction-date rows: canonical date, customer id, and transaction amount. One row for each transaction record in customer_transactions with txn_date cast to ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

views.name: customer_daily_balance_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  ct.txn_date AS txn_date,
  SUM(ct.txn_amount) AS daily_net_txn,
  (
    SELECT SUM(t2.txn_amount)
    FROM customer_transactions t2
    WHERE t2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
      AND t2.txn_date <= ct.txn_date
  ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM customer_transactions ct
GROUP BY
  ct.customer_id,
  ct.txn_date
views.description: Running cumulative balance per customer per date computed from customer_transactions. Aggregates multiple transactions on the same date into a single date-level net txn_amount, then computes running sum ordered by date per customer. Does not enforce non-negative floor or fill missing dates; produces one row per customer_id + txn_date with cumulative_balance.

views.name: customer_monthly_max_daily_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.customer_id AS customer_id,
  strftime('%Y-%m', d.calendar_date) AS month,
  MAX(d.end_of_day_balance) AS max_daily_balance
FROM customer_daily_end_balance d
GROUP BY d.customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', d.calendar_date)
views.description: Per-customer per-calendar-month maximum of the customer's daily balance within that month. Intended to be computed after filling missing dates and enforcing non-negative daily balances; this view assumes input daily balances are available (e.g. from filled/carry-forwarded daily series). Exposes month in 'YYYY-MM' format, customer_id and that customer's max_daily_balance for the month.

views.name: shopping_cart_events_mapped
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.visit_id,
  e.cookie_id,
  e.page_id,
  p.product_id,
  p.page_name,
  e.event_type,
  i.event_name,
  e.sequence_number,
  e.event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events e
JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p
  ON e.page_id = p.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier i
  ON e.event_type = i.event_type
WHERE e.page_id IS NOT NULL
  AND p.product_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: All shopping cart event rows enriched with their page metadata and normalized event_name label from the event identifier table; excludes events with NULL product_id. Keeps event timestamps and visit/cookie identifiers so time-based comparisons (later purchases) can be computed downstream.

views.name: product_page_catalog
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id AS TEXT) AS product_id,
  shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.page_id AS page_id,
  shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.page_name AS product_name
FROM shopping_cart_page_hierarchy
WHERE shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical list of product identifiers and their human-readable page_name (product_name). Normalizes page_id <-> product_id mapping and preserves page_name, allowing lookup of product metadata. Useful for joining product-level metrics back to names.

views.name: interest_monthly_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  interest_metrics.interest_id AS interest_id,
  interest_metrics.month_year AS month_year,
  interest_metrics.composition AS composition,
  interest_metrics.index_value AS index_value,
  (interest_metrics.composition / interest_metrics.index_value) AS composition_over_index
FROM interest_metrics
WHERE interest_metrics.index_value IS NOT NULL
  AND interest_metrics.index_value != 0
views.description: Normalized monthly metrics per interest: keep one row per interest per month with numeric composition and index_value and a canonical month_year string. Excludes rows with NULL or zero index_value to avoid division-by-zero.

views.name: interest_id_to_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  im.id AS interest_id,
  im.interest_name AS interest_name
FROM interest_map im
views.description: Mapping from interest_id in interest_metrics to interest_name from interest_map. One row per interest id (using interest_map.id) with stable name fields for joining/labeling.

views.name: monthly_top_interest
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.month_year AS month_year,
  MIN(m.interest_id) AS top_interest_id,
  MAX(m.composition_over_index) AS max_composition_over_index
FROM
  interest_monthly_metrics AS m
GROUP BY
  m.month_year
views.description: For each month (month_year) compute the interest_id with the maximum composition_over_index. If ties occur, pick the smallest interest_id. Produces one row per month with the top interest_id and its max composition_over_index.

views.name: interest_metrics_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(_month AS INTEGER) AS _month,
  CAST(_year AS INTEGER) AS _year,
  month_year,
  CAST(interest_id AS INTEGER) AS interest_id,
  composition,
  index_value,
  ranking,
  percentile_ranking
FROM interest_metrics
views.description: Canonicalized rows from interest_metrics exposing month, year, interest id and composition/index measures. Keeps one row per original interest_metrics row (no aggregation) and casts month/year to numeric columns for ordering.

views.name: interest_max_composition_per_interest
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  interest_id,
  MAX(composition) AS max_composition
FROM interest_metrics
GROUP BY interest_id
views.description: For each interest_id, compute the maximum composition observed. Produces one row per interest_id with the max composition value. Does not yet pick the month-year tie-breaker row.

views.name: interest_max_row_with_tiebreak
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  imr.month_year AS month_year,
  imr.interest_id AS interest_id,
  imr.composition AS composition,
  imr._year AS _year,
  imr._month AS _month
FROM interest_metrics_rows imr
JOIN interest_max_composition_per_interest imax
  ON imr.interest_id = imax.interest_id
  AND imr.composition = imax.max_composition
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM interest_metrics_rows imr2
  WHERE imr2.interest_id = imr.interest_id
    AND imr2.composition = imr.composition
    AND (
      imr2._year > imr._year
      OR (imr2._year = imr._year AND imr2._month > imr._month)
    )
)
views.description: Selects, for each interest_id, the single row that represents that interest's maximum composition. If multiple rows tie on composition, picks the row with the most recent year (_year) then most recent month (_month). Outputs the month_year for the chosen row along with composition and interest_id.

views.name: bitcoin_txn_buy_with_member_region_and_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bt.txn_id AS txn_id,
  bt.member_id AS member_id,
  bm.region AS region,
  bt.ticker AS ticker,
  bt.txn_date AS txn_date,
  CAST(substr(bt.txn_date, -4) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
  bt.quantity AS quantity,
  bt.txn_type AS txn_type
FROM bitcoin_transactions bt
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members bm
  ON bt.member_id = bm.member_id
WHERE bt.txn_type = 'BUY'
views.description: One row per bitcoin_transactions BUY transaction, joined to bitcoin_members to expose member region and with calendar year extracted from txn_date. Normalizes txn_date year as integer and keeps quantity and ticker for later price joins.

views.name: bitcoin_price_by_ticker_and_market_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker,
  market_date,
  CAST(price AS REAL) AS price
FROM bitcoin_prices
WHERE price IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical price lookup by ticker and market_date (market_date kept in original format). Exposes price as numeric for joining to transactions to compute USD spent.

views.name: region_year_buy_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  btxn.region AS region,
  btxn.calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  SUM(btxn.quantity) AS total_quantity_btc,
  SUM(btxn.quantity * COALESCE(bprice.price, 0.0)) AS total_spent_usd,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(btxn.quantity) > 0 THEN SUM(btxn.quantity * COALESCE(bprice.price, 0.0)) / SUM(btxn.quantity)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS avg_purchase_price_usd_per_btc
FROM
  bitcoin_txn_buy_with_member_region_and_year btxn
LEFT JOIN
  bitcoin_price_by_ticker_and_market_date bprice
  ON btxn.ticker = bprice.ticker
     AND btxn.txn_date = bprice.market_date
WHERE
  btxn.txn_type = 'BUY'
GROUP BY
  btxn.region,
  btxn.calendar_year
HAVING
  SUM(btxn.quantity) > 0

semantic_filters.total_quantity_btc: > 0 (logical filter to be applied in query; stored as a note)

views.description: Aggregated BUY measures per region and calendar_year: total BTC quantity bought and total USD spent (computed as price * quantity after joining to btc price view). Does not apply exclusion of earliest year per region; keeps rows where total_quantity_btc > 0.
